I will keep things simple and low-risk. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so the crop pattern I trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. At my age, I would not spread myself across too many crops or try something unfamiliar. Wheat and maize fit my local weather, local soils, local machinery, and the way water is usually managed here. I know how to grow them, I can get seed and inputs easily, and I can sell them without trouble.

I will plant improved winter wheat for stable yield and strong adaptation, then hybrid summer maize after wheat harvest because maize responds well to fertilizer and usually gives better production. I will use moderate fertilizer, not excessive amounts, because I want dependable yields without wasting money. I will plough before wheat to break the soil and help the next crop establish well, and after wheat harvest I will use rotary tillage for maize so I can turn the crop around fast. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in this area depends more on timely water at key stages. I will also keep pesticide use limited to what is needed, because too many sprays cost money and add work. My whole plan is to stay with the rotation I understand best, protect yield, control labor, and avoid unnecessary risk.
